THEORY-GUIDED LSTM FOR SUSTAINABLE WATER RESOURCE MANAGEMENT: THE JOUMINE–GHEZALA RESERVOIR SYSTEM, TUNISIA

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)

ABSTRACT

Managing parallel reservoir systems efficiently is essential for securing urban water supplies in water-scarce, semi-arid regions. Standard machine learning models, however, often generate operational rules that ignore physical laws, leading to unrealistic predictions. To address this limitation, this study proposes a Theory-Guided Long Short-Term Memory (TG-LSTM) framework for the coordinated operation of parallel water-supply reservoir groups — to the best of the authors’ knowledge, the first application of this approach to such a reservoir configuration. The framework incorporates domain knowledge directly into the model training process: equal spill and dead storage probabilities are enforced across member reservoirs to balance system-wide risk, while physical storage limits and downstream supply constraints are embedded into the loss function as penalty terms. The model was validated on 35 years of daily operational data (1988–2022) from the Joumine–Ghezala reservoir system in northern Tunisia, which supplies the Greater Bizerte urban area. The fully integrated TG-LSTM outperformed all baseline configurations, achieving Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) values of 0.82 and 0.80 for the Joumine and Ghezala reservoirs, respectively, during independent testing. Importantly, while standard data-driven models produced physically impossible outputs — such as negative storage levels and supply over-allocation during the 2002 and 2016–2017 drought periods — the TG-LSTM maintained mass balance at all times and eliminated all infeasible operational outcomes. This framework offers a reliable and physically consistent tool for the joint scheduling of multi-reservoir systems under increasing hydrometeorological stress.
